residencyRequirements.description: Either spouse must be domiciled in New Zealand at the time of the application (Family Proceedings Act 1980, s.38). Domicile is distinct from residency — it means NZ is the person's permanent home.

waitingPeriod.description: No waiting period after the order is made. A dissolution order takes effect immediately upon being granted (Family Proceedings Act 1980, s.46). However, the 2-year separation must be completed before the application is filed.

noFault.name: Two-Year Separation
noFault.description: The marriage has broken down irreconcilably, as shown by the parties having lived apart for 2 or more years immediately preceding the filing of the application.

noFault.name: Family Violence (Protected Person)
noFault.description: A protected person with a final protection order (or registered foreign protection order) against their spouse may apply for dissolution without the 2-year separation requirement. In effect from 17 October 2025.
noFault.statute: Family Proceedings Act 1980, s.39A (inserted by Family Proceedings (Dissolution of Marriage or Civil Union for Family Violence) Amendment Act 2024)

basic.name: Application for Dissolution of Marriage
basic.description: Filed in the Family Court under the Family Proceedings Act 1980; available as a sole or joint application

basic.name: Affidavit in Support of Application
basic.description: Sworn affidavit confirming the 2-year separation and other required facts

legalCitations.description: Governs dissolution of marriage in New Zealand
Division of relationship property — equal sharing starting point
Guardianship, day-to-day care, and contact arrangements for children
Framework for child support assessment and collection by Inland Revenue
Governs protection orders and the legal response to family violence (replaced the Domestic Violence Act 1995)

legalCitations.code: Family Proceedings (Dissolution of Marriage or Civil Union for Family Violence) Amendment Act 2024
legalCitations.description: Allows dissolution without 2-year separation for protected persons with a final protection order (in force 17 October 2025)

filingFees.notes: Filing fee for dissolution application (updated per Ministry of Justice). Fee waiver may be available for applicants who cannot afford the fee. Contact the Family Court registry for current fees.

childSupportGuidelines.notes: Child support is assessed by Inland Revenue using a formula based on parents' income, care arrangements, and number of children. It is separate from the dissolution process.

spousalSupportGuidelines.notes: Maintenance is based on the reasonable needs of the applicant and the ability of the other spouse to pay. It is not automatic and must be specifically applied for.

effectiveDateRule: The dissolution order takes effect immediately upon being made by the court (Family Proceedings Act 1980, s.46). There is no further waiting period after the order is granted.
certificateNote: A certificate confirming the dissolution may be obtained from the Family Court registry after the order takes effect.
